# AI Teammate — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# ROLLOUT SCOPE (this phase): the loop reacts ONLY to artifacts authored
# by the machine itself — issues opened by `ai-teammate` and PRs opened
# by `ai-teammate`. Human-created issues (even labeled/assigned to the
# agent) do NOT trigger anything yet; that gate opens in a later phase.
#
#   issue ASSIGNED to ai-teammate   → factory, leg=dev (fresh handoff)
#   issue labeled while assigned     → factory, leg derived by the guard
#   PR opened by ai-teammate         → factory, leg=review on the linked
#                                      issue (parsed from the PR body)
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual)  → leg pinned by input
#
# ALL loop logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
# event triggers, the author filter, the PR→issue resolution, the
# per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
# Secrets (explicit mapping): SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required by the factory),
# ZAI_CODE_KEY, KIMI_REVIEW_KEY (optional provider keys).
# Vars: FA_VERSION_MACHINE || FA_VERSION || latest, DMTOOLS_VERSION,
# MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS.

name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      ((github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' &&
       format('▶ {0} (SM) · pr-{1}', github.event.inputs.leg, github.event.inputs.pr) ||
       format('▶ {0} (SM) · gh-{1}', github.event.inputs.leg, github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      format('{0} · gh-{1}: {2}',
        github.event.action == 'assigned' && '⚒️ dev (assigned handoff)' || 'machine loop',
        github.event.issue.number, github.event.issue.title) }}

on:
  issues:
    # assigned only — labeled REMOVED (2026-10-01): every label echo (the dev
    # leg's own status:In Development, SM backfills) spawned a queued twin run
    # behind the per-issue concurrency group (live dmd gh-317/gh-318); the
    # in-run dedupe cannot act — workflow-level concurrency holds the whole
    # run pending before any job starts. Leg dispatching is dispatch-only
    # (SM workflow_dispatch; manual rework override #544 = dispatch leg=rework).
    types: [assigned]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored review runs (#687) — the SM dispatches review with pr instead of issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

# Explicit top-level permissions, minimal read: job-level grants below carry
# the real rights (SEC-08 review #849, thread -1oD — a top-level write block
# becomes the default for every future job in this workflow). The factory
# job's own permissions block mirrors the pinned callee's declared scopes
# (factory-teammate.yml declares contents/issues/pull-requests/actions
# write): a reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above the CALLING JOB's
# effective grant, so an explicit read-only block ON THE CALLING JOB made
# every call fail validation with startup_failure (live bisect,
# 2026-09-18) — the job-scoped mirror is the minimal consistent set (SEC-08,
# #796).
permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-266');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # Assignment gate. Runs ONLY when the issue is assigned to `ai-teammate`
  # (the human handoff) or on explicit dispatch (SM ticks). Everything else
  # exits empty and the factory job is skipped. PRs do NOT trigger this
  # workflow: the loop's review/rework legs are driven by SM ticks and
  # issue labels, and pull_request-triggered runs of this stub validated
  # as startup_failure on PRs #624/#625 (red-X noise with no value).
  gate:
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' && contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    # Read-only: this job only resolves assignees/inputs and echoes outputs.
    # It inherits the workflow-level read-only default and must NOT see the
    # factory job's write scopes (SEC-08 review, #796).
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      issue: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.issue }}
      leg: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.leg }}
    steps:
      - name: Resolve target issue and leg for this event
        id: resolve
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          ACTION: ${{ github.event.action }}
          NUMBER: ${{ github.event.number }}
          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          case "$EVENT" in
            workflow_dispatch)
              # Manual/SM dispatch: inputs flow straight through.
              echo "issue=${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"   # empty here; factory takes inputs.issue
              echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              ;;
            issues)
              # Assignment-driven loop: a fresh `assigned` event (human
              # handoff) → dev leg; `labeled` (agent:review / agent:rework
              # added by the machine itself while assigned) → guard derives.
              # POLICY (#693 steering): dev fires ONLY when ai-teammate is
              # the sole assignee — any human assignee owns the issue and
              # the machine stands by for reviews instead (review paths:
              # review-external-once / agent:review on the eventual PR).
              if [ "$ACTION" = "assigned" ]; then
                HUMAN=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/${ISSUE_NUMBER}" \
                  --jq '[.assignees[].login] | map(select(. != "ai-teammate")) | length')
                if [ "$HUMAN" = "0" ]; then
                  echo "leg=dev" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                else
                  echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                  echo "::notice title=machine-standby::issue #${ISSUE_NUMBER} has a human assignee — no dev, review-only"
                fi
              else
                echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              fi
              echo "issue=${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              ;;
          esac
          echo "→ gate done (see outputs)"

  factory:
    needs: gate
    # Dispatch runs carry the target in inputs (gate outputs are empty by
    # design there); event runs carry it in gate outputs.
    if: needs.gate.result == 'success' && (needs.gate.outputs.issue != '' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
    # Job-scoped grants mirroring the pinned callee's declared scopes (a
    # reusable call is capped by the calling job's effective permissions —
    # see the top-level comment). Scoped to THIS job so any future job in
    # this workflow defaults to the top-level read-only.
    permissions:
      contents: write         # the factory pushes branches / session trees
      issues: write           # labels, comments, close-issue safety net
      pull-requests: write    # PR creation, review threads, update-branch
      actions: write          # actions/cache save phase + workflow_dispatch
    # Tracks dmtools-agentic-workflows @main — always-latest policy (owner
    # directive 2026-10-04): awf main is load-bearing and review-gated, so
    # awf fixes (teammate defaults awf#12, kicker real ticks awf#13,
    # per-SHA concurrency awf#14) go live on merge, no re-pin ceremony.
    # Accept…

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# ROLLOUT SCOPE (this phase): the loop reacts ONLY to artifacts authored
# by the machine itself — issues opened by `ai-teammate` and PRs opened
# by `ai-teammate`. Human-created issues (even labeled/assigned to the
# agent) do NOT trigger anything yet; that gate opens in a later phase.
#
#   issue ASSIGNED to ai-teammate   → factory, leg=dev (fresh handoff)
#   issue labeled while assigned     → factory, leg derived by the guard
#   PR opened by ai-teammate         → factory, leg=review on the linked
#                                      issue (parsed from the PR body)
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual)  → leg pinned by input
#
# ALL loop logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
# event triggers, the author filter, the PR→issue resolution, the
# per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
# Secrets (explicit mapping): SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required by the factory),
# ZAI_CODE_KEY, KIMI_REVIEW_KEY (optional provider keys).
# Vars: FA_VERSION_MACHINE || FA_VERSION || latest, DMTOOLS_VERSION,
# MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS.

name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      ((github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' &&
       format('▶ {0} (SM) · pr-{1}', github.event.inputs.leg, github.event.inputs.pr) ||
       format('▶ {0} (SM) · gh-{1}', github.event.inputs.leg, github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      format('{0} · gh-{1}: {2}',
        github.event.action == 'assigned' && '⚒️ dev (assigned handoff)' || 'machine loop',
        github.event.issue.number, github.event.issue.title) }}

on:
  issues:
    # assigned only — labeled REMOVED (2026-10-01): every label echo (the dev
    # leg's own status:In Development, SM backfills) spawned a queued twin run
    # behind the per-issue concurrency group (live dmd gh-317/gh-318); the
    # in-run dedupe cannot act — workflow-level concurrency holds the whole
    # run pending before any job starts. Leg dispatching is dispatch-only
    # (SM workflow_dispatch; manual rework override #544 = dispatch leg=rework).
    types: [assigned]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored review runs (#687) — the SM dispatches review with pr instead of issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

# Explicit top-level permissions, minimal read: job-level grants below carry
# the real rights (SEC-08 review #849, thread -1oD — a top-level write block
# becomes the default for every future job in this workflow). The factory
# job's own permissions block mirrors the pinned callee's declared scopes
# (factory-teammate.yml declares contents/issues/pull-requests/actions
# write): a reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above the CALLING JOB's
# effective grant, so an explicit read-only block ON THE CALLING JOB made
# every call fail validation with startup_failure (live bisect,
# 2026-09-18) — the job-scoped mirror is the minimal consistent set (SEC-08,
# #796).
permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-266');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # Assignment gate. Runs ONLY when the issue is assigned to `ai-teammate`
  # (the human handoff) or on explicit dispatch (SM ticks). Everything else
  # exits empty and the factory job is skipped. PRs do NOT trigger this
  # workflow: the loop's review/rework legs are driven by SM ticks and
  # issue labels, and pull_request-triggered runs of this stub validated
  # as startup_failure on PRs #624/#625 (red-X noise with no value).
  gate:
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' && contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    # Read-only: this job only resolves assignees/inputs and echoes outputs.
    # It inherits the workflow-level read-only default and must NOT see the
    # factory job's write scopes (SEC-08 review, #796).
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      issue: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.issue }}
      leg: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.leg }}
    steps:
      - name: Resolve target issue and leg for this event
        id: resolve
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          ACTION: ${{ github.event.action }}
          NUMBER: ${{ github.event.number }}
          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          case "$EVENT" in
            workflow_dispatch)
              # Manual/SM dispatch: inputs flow straight through.
              echo "issue=${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"   # empty here; factory takes inputs.issue
              echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              ;;
            issues)
              # Assignment-driven loop: a fresh `assigned` event (human
              # handoff) → dev leg; `labeled` (agent:review / agent:rework
              # added by the machine itself while assigned) → guard derives.
              # POLICY (#693 steering): dev fires ONLY when ai-teammate is
              # the sole assignee — any human assignee owns the issue and
              # the machine stands by for reviews instead (review paths:
              # review-external-once / agent:review on the eventual PR).
              if [ "$ACTION" = "assigned" ]; then
                HUMAN=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/${ISSUE_NUMBER}" \
                  --jq '[.assignees[].login] | map(select(. != "ai-teammate")) | length')
                if [ "$HUMAN" = "0" ]; then
                  echo "leg=dev" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                else
                  echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                  echo "::notice title=machine-standby::issue #${ISSUE_NUMBER} has a human assignee — no dev, review-only"
                fi
              else
                echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              fi
              echo "issue=${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              ;;
          esac
          echo "→ gate done (see outputs)"

  factory:
    needs: gate
    # Dispatch runs carry the target in inputs (gate outputs are empty by
    # design there); event runs carry it in gate outputs.
    if: needs.gate.result == 'success' && (needs.gate.outputs.issue != '' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
    # Job-scoped grants mirroring the pinned callee's declared scopes (a
    # reusable call is capped by the calling job's effective permissions —
    # see the top-level comment). Scoped to THIS job so any future job in
    # this workflow defaults to the top-level read-only.
    permissions:
      contents: write         # the factory pushes branches / session trees
      issues: write           # labels, comments, close-issue safety net
      pull-requests: write    # PR creation, review threads, update-branch
      actions: write          # actions/cache save phase + workflow_dispatch
    # Tracks dmtools-agentic-workflows @main — always-latest policy (owner
    # directive 2026-10-04): awf main is load-bearing and review-gated, so
    # awf fixes (teammate defaults awf#12, kicker real ticks awf#13,
    # per-SHA concurrency awf#14) go live on merge, no re-pin ceremony.
    # Accept…

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

blocks.text:
# AI Teammate — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# ROLLOUT SCOPE (this phase): the loop reacts ONLY to artifacts authored
# by the machine itself — issues opened by `ai-teammate` and PRs opened
# by `ai-teammate`. Human-created issues (even labeled/assigned to the
# agent) do NOT trigger anything yet; that gate opens in a later phase.
#
#   issue ASSIGNED to ai-teammate   → factory, leg=dev (fresh handoff)
#   issue labeled while assigned     → factory, leg derived by the guard
#   PR opened by ai-teammate         → factory, leg=review on the linked
#                                      issue (parsed from the PR body)
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual)  → leg pinned by input
#
# ALL loop logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
# event triggers, the author filter, the PR→issue resolution, the
# per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
# Secrets (explicit mapping): SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required by the factory),
# ZAI_CODE_KEY, KIMI_REVIEW_KEY (optional provider keys).
# Vars: FA_VERSION_MACHINE || FA_VERSION || latest, DMTOOLS_VERSION,
# MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS.

name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      ((github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' &&
       format('▶ {0} (SM) · pr-{1}', github.event.inputs.leg, github.event.inputs.pr) ||
       format('▶ {0} (SM) · gh-{1}', github.event.inputs.leg, github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      format('{0} · gh-{1}: {2}',
        github.event.action == 'assigned' && '⚒️ dev (assigned handoff)' || 'machine loop',
        github.event.issue.number, github.event.issue.title) }}

on:
  issues:
    # assigned only — labeled REMOVED (2026-10-01): every label echo (the dev
    # leg's own status:In Development, SM backfills) spawned a queued twin run
    # behind the per-issue concurrency group (live dmd gh-317/gh-318); the
    # in-run dedupe cannot act — workflow-level concurrency holds the whole
    # run pending before any job starts. Leg dispatching is dispatch-only
    # (SM workflow_dispatch; manual rework override #544 = dispatch leg=rework).
    types: [assigned]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored review runs (#687) — the SM dispatches review with pr instead of issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

# Explicit top-level permissions, minimal read: job-level grants below carry
# the real rights (SEC-08 review #849, thread -1oD — a top-level write block
# becomes the default for every future job in this workflow). The factory
# job's own permissions block mirrors the pinned callee's declared scopes
# (factory-teammate.yml declares contents/issues/pull-requests/actions
# write): a reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above the CALLING JOB's
# effective grant, so an explicit read-only block ON THE CALLING JOB made
# every call fail validation with startup_failure (live bisect,
# 2026-09-18) — the job-scoped mirror is the minimal consistent set (SEC-08,
# #796).
permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-266');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # Assignment gate. Runs ONLY when the issue is assigned to `ai-teammate`
  # (the human handoff) or on explicit dispatch (SM ticks). Everything else
  # exits empty and the factory job is skipped. PRs do NOT trigger this
  # workflow: the loop's review/rework legs are driven by SM ticks and
  # issue labels, and pull_request-triggered runs of this stub validated
  # as startup_failure on PRs #624/#625 (red-X noise with no value).
  gate:
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' && contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    # Read-only: this job only resolves assignees/inputs and echoes outputs.
    # It inherits the workflow-level read-only default and must NOT see the
    # factory job's write scopes (SEC-08 review, #796).
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      issue: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.issue }}
      leg: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.leg }}
    steps:
      - name: Resolve target issue and leg for this event
        id: resolve
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          ACTION: ${{ github.event.action }}
          NUMBER: ${{ github.event.number }}
          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          case "$EVENT" in
            workflow_dispatch)
              # Manual/SM dispatch: inputs flow straight through.
              echo "issue=${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"   # empty here; factory takes inputs.issue
              echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

# Factory · AI Teammate leg — REUSABLE workflow (dmtools-agents factory pack, top-level: GitHub requires reusable workflows at the .github/workflows root — no subdirectories).
#
# The dev→review→rework machine loop for GitHub-issues trackers, hosted in
# dmtools-agents so target repositories carry only a thin stub (event
# triggers + this call) plus .dmtools/config.js, secrets and vars. Runs in
# the CALLER's context: github.repository = the target repo; vars.* and
# secrets.* resolve from the caller (each target pins its own versions).
#
# Legs (guard derives the slot when `leg` is empty):
#   bug | story | review | rework — the runner configs live in the TARGET repo
#   (.dmtools/runners/*), wired via .dmtools/config.js sm.runners.
#
# Loop mechanics (identical to the dmtools-dart template this was ported
# from — see that file's history for the full rationale):
#   issue assigned/labeled → guard → ticket input → dmtools run <runner>
#   → agent develops → PR ("Closes #NN") → review verdict step:
#       APPROVE + green PR checks → pr_approved → merge (merge-trigger/stub)
#       CHANGES_REQUESTED        → agent:rework (bounded: MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS,
#                                  then needs-human escalation)
#   Review/rework queue labels are stripped at cycle end (no self-loops).
#   fa sessions ride the fa-sess/gh-<n> branch (cache saves are denied on
#   issues-event runs); fa project memory is committed back to the repo.
#
# Secrets (via `secrets: inherit`): SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (PAT — labels added
#   with GITHUB_TOKEN never fire `labeled` events; pushes must not author
#   as github-actions[bot]), ZAI_CODE_KEY, KIMI_REVIEW_KEY.
# Vars: FA_VERSION_MACHINE || FA_VERSION || latest, DMTOOLS_VERSION,
#   MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS (default 2).
#
# Caller stub:
#   on:
#     issues: {types: [assigned, labeled]}
#     workflow_dispatch: {inputs: {issue: {type: number}, leg: {type: string}}}
#   concurrency:
#     group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue }}
#     cancel-in-progress: false
#   jobs:
#     factory:
#       uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@<ref>
#       with:
#         issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue }}
#         leg: ${{ inputs.leg || '' }}
#         reason: ${{ inputs.reason || 'stub' }}
#       secrets: inherit

name: 'Factory · AI Teammate'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      # The ref THIS awf repo was invoked at — a reusable workflow runs in
      # the CALLER's context, so github.workflow_ref carries the caller's ref
      # (dart's branch), which is meaningless against the awf remote. The
      # stub passes its own pin here (main in production) — same pattern as
      factory_home_ref:
        description: Awf ref the caller pinned factory-teammate.yml to
        type: string
        required: false
        default: main
      runner:
        description: 'Runner label (self-hosted pools must be visible to the CALLING org)'
        type: string
        default: 'ubuntu-slim'
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (string: number-typed reusable inputs cannot take expressions). Empty when pr is given (PR-anchored run, #687).'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687). Exactly one of issue|pr must be set.'
        required: false
        type: string
      machine-author:
        description: "Deployment's machine (bot) login (#687): gates rework re-arm in PR-anchored reviews (auto-approve via pr_approved is author-agnostic per the owner rule). Injected as jobParams.machineAuthor — branch-independent (the checked-out PR branch carries no machineAuthor config)."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: "Which leg to run: dev | review | rework (empty = derive from labels/assignees)"
        required: false
        type: string
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      factory_ref:
        # TEMPORARY no-op (2026-10-16 incident: legs startup_fail while
        # callers still send it — fa wrapper fix in flight, agents done in
        # #931). Remove AGAIN only after EVERY caller stops passing it.
        description: 'Deprecated, unread no-op. Do not use.'
        required: false
        default: ''
        type: string
      # Optional agent-work toolchains (salvaged from #35): "" (default)
      # installs NOTHING — explicit opt-in per caller. The dmtools engine
      # and its dart runtime are installed by install-dmtools-cli.sh and
      # are NEVER gated on these inputs.
      java-version:
        description: 'JDK for agent work (Temurin, Gradle/Maven cache). "" (default) installs NOTHING. e.g. "21".'
        required: false
        default: ''
        type: string
      node-version:
        description: 'Node.js for agent work (npm cache). "" (default) installs NOTHING. e.g. "20".'
        required: false
        default: ''
        type: string
      python-version:
        description: 'Python for agent work. "" (default) installs NOTHING. e.g. "3.12".'
        required: false
        default: ''
        type: string
      flutter-version:
        description: 'Flutter SDK for agent work (cached). "" (default) installs NOTHING — most consumers are not Flutter projects and bring their own toolchain via the setup/install scripts. A value installs Flutter+matching Dart via flutter-action with SDK caching (e.g. "stable", "3.38.0"); Flutter targets (fa) pass it explicitly.'
        required: false
        default: ''
        type: string

      CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY1_NAME:
        description: 'Env var name for slot 1 (plain input, not secret).'
        required: false
        type: string
      CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY2_NAME:
        description: 'Env var name for slot 2 (plain input, not secret).'
        required: false
        type: string
      CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY3_NAME:
        description: 'Env var name for slot 3 (plain input, not secret).'
        required: false
        type: string

    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN:
        description: 'PAT with repo scope — machine labels, pushes, PR/issue API (secrets: inherit does not cross repository boundaries).'
        required: true
      ZAI_CODE_KEY:
        description: 'z.ai API key (dev/rework provider + review queue fallback)'
        required: false
      KIMI_REVIEW_KEY:
        description: 'kimi API key (review provider, first in the queue)'
        required: false
      CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY1:
        description: 'Generic provider-key slot 1 — value lands in the agent job env under CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY1_NAME. The factory never knows key names; the caller stub documents which repo secret maps here.'
        required: false
      CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY2:
        description: 'Generic provider-key slot 2 — see CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY1.'
        required: false
      CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY3:
        description: 'Generic provider-key slot 3 — see CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY1.'
        required: false

# NOTE: no `concurrency` here — the caller stub owns the per-issue group.
# A reusable workflow with the SAME group as its caller deadlocks: the caller
# holds the group while the called workflow waits for it forever (pending, 0 jobs).

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write
  # actions/cache@v6 save phase needs actions:write on github.token.
  actions: write

jobs:
  guard:
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner || 'ubuntu-slim' }}
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.check.outputs.run }}
      runner: ${{ steps.check.outputs.runner }}
      config: ${{ steps.check.outputs.config }}
      kind: ${{ steps.check.outputs.kind }}
      anchor: ${{ steps.check.outputs.anchor }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout target repository (config, runners)
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          # caller-repo checkout: the factory reads .dmtools/config.js from
          # the TARGET repository, never from the factory pack
          ref: ${{ github.ref }}
          # gate job only: config.js at the head + API guards — no git
          # history walks. fetch-depth 0 cloned the FULL history here
          # (~1 min on fa, every leg) for nothing.
          fetch-depth: 1
      - name: Set up Java for agent work
        if: inputs.java-version != ''
        uses: actions/setup-java@v5
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: ${{ inputs.java-version }}
          cache: gradle
      - name: Set up Node.js for agent work
        if: inputs.node-version != ''
        uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: ${{ inputs.node-version }}
      - name: Set up Python for agent work
        if: inputs.python-version != ''
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ inputs.python-version }}
      - name: Fetch factory scripts (this repo @ invocation ref)
        # Stage-2 de-bloat delivery: the guard's domain step (scripts/
        # teammate-dispatch-gate.sh) rides the same immutable factory-kit
        # fetch as the teammate job — scripts/ is checked out at EXACTLY the
        # ref the caller invoked (github.workflow_ref), so the gate logic can
        # never skew from the workflow version that calls it. Strict, unlike
        # the teammate fetch: the guard has no FACTORY_ROOT fallback, so a
        # failed delivery must red the run, not silently skip the gate.
        env:
          AWF_REF: ${{ inputs.factory_home_ref }}
        run: |
          ref="$AWF_REF"
          dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit"
          git init -q "$dir"
          git -C "$dir" remote add origin https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows.git
          git -C "$dir" fetch -q --depth 1 origin "$ref" \
            || { echo "::error::factory scripts fetch failed at $ref — the dispatch gate cannot run"; exit 1; }
          git -C "$dir" checkout -q FETCH_HEAD -- scripts/
          [ -f "$dir/scripts/teammate-dispatch-gate.sh" ] \
            || { echo "::error::scripts/teammate-dispatch-gate.sh missing at $ref"; exit 1; }
      - name: Decide whether this event is for the agent
        id: check
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          NUMBER: ${{ inputs.issue }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ inputs.pr }}
          # Event context rides through from the caller (issues events) —
          # empty for pure dispatches. The guard ALWAYS refreshes from the
          # API (queued runs see a stale payload); this is only a fallback.
          ASSIGNEES: ${{ join(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, ' ') }}
          LABELS: ${{ join(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, ' ') }}
          ACTOR: ${{ github.event.action || github.event_name }}
          # #544: the `labeled` event sender — the owner-override gate checks
          # its repo permission before honoring a manual agent:rework.
          # Empty for schedule-scan dispatches (SM ticks): the label is
          # trusted as-is there (see rework_override_ok below).
          SENDER: ${{ github.event.sender.login || '' }}
          INPUT_LEG: ${{ inputs.leg }}
          INPUT_REASON: ${{ inputs.reason }}
          # The assignee gate below compares against the machine login.
          # AGENT_HANDLE lives on the TEAMMATE job's env — without it here
          # the guard's $AGENT_HANDLE is empty, `grep -w` never matches, and
          # assignment-triggered dev legs never start (live: dmtools-dart
          # run 35519287617 — issue #173 assigned to ai-teammate → skipped).
          AGENT_HANDLE: ai-teammate
        # Body: scripts/teammate-dispatch-gate.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/teammate-dispatch-gate.sh"

  teammate:
    needs: guard
    if: needs.guard.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner || 'ubuntu-slim' }}
    # A real fix is a 40-80 minute agent session (gh-623 burned a full RCA +
    # TDD cycle at exactly 61 minutes and the job was killed mid-work); dev
    # legs over Flutter sources run the analyzer + full flutter test suite
    # and live 2-3 hours (fa gh-1077 leg was killed mid-work at exactly 110
    # on 2026-09-30). The autocommit timer (300s) bounds the blast radius of
    # a kill; this timeout bounds the bill.
    timeout-minutes: 260
    # Workflow-level env is NOT supported in reusable (workflow_call)
    # workflows — the factory failed validation at startup until this
    # moved down to the job.
    env:
      AGENT_HANDLE: ai-teammate
      FA_VERSION: ${{ vars.FA_VERSION_MACHINE || vars.FA_VERSION || 'latest' }}
      DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'latest' }}
      MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS: ${{ vars.MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS || 2 }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout target repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          # NO submodules and NO agents fetch here: the factory works with
          # RELEASES (factory kit + per-agent packs), it never materializes
          # the dmtools-agents tree in leg worktrees — that tree is the
          # integration-TEST target's own business (epam/dmtools-dart#412
          # fetches dmtools-agents@main in its own quality.yml).
          # Materializing agents/ here produced embedded-repo gitlinks
          # (dart ai/gh-379, fa ai/gh-1646/1643, 2026-10-16).
          persist-credentials: false


      - name: "Fetch factory kit (this repo @ invocation ref — immutable)"
        # Trust-boundary scripts (git push guard, source PAT credentials)
        # ride the SAME immutable ref the caller invoked this workflow at
        # (github.workflow_ref = owner/repo/.github/workflows/<name>.yml@<ref>)
        # — a PR head can no longer supply them (self-host security,
        # 2026-10-01) and the script version can never skew from the workflow
        # version that calls it. Plain git (no action): GitLab-portable.
        #
        # RUNNER_TEMP, never $GITHUB_WORKSPACE: a nested git repo inside the
        # workspace poisons every downstream `git add` (the gitlink "does
        # not have a commit checked out", exit 128 — live fa gh-1000
        # 2026-10-03: PR staging, origin-sync clean-tree gate, and the
        # session timer auto-commit all tripped on it).
        env:
          AWF_REF: ${{ inputs.factory_home_ref }}
        run: |
          ref="$AWF_REF"
          dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit"
          git init -q "$dir"
          git -C "$dir" remote add origin https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows.git
          git -C "$dir" fetch -q --depth 1 origin "$ref" \
            || { echo "::warning::kit fetch failed — falling back to FACTORY_ROOT copies"; exit 0; }
          git -C "$dir" checkout -q FETCH_HEAD -- kit/
          git -C "$dir" checkout -q FETCH_HEAD -- scripts/ 2>/dev/null || true  # stage-1 de-bloat: step bodies live in scripts/ (same immutable ref)
          [ -f "$dir/kit/git-push-guard.sh" ] || { echo "::warning::kit incomplete at $ref — falling back"; rm -rf "$dir"; exit 0; }
          # Kit liveness probe (awf#7): a guard whose shebang is not line 1
          # silently executes under /bin/sh and dies with "Syntax error" on
          # every git call — the whole dev session loses git (branch setup,
          # timer auto-commit, PR post-action) with quiet skips downstream.
          head -1 "$dir/kit/git-push-guard.sh" | grep -q '^#!.*bash' \
            || { echo "::error::kit git-push-guard.sh lost its shebang (line 1) at $ref — refusing to arm a broken guard"; exit 1; }
          cp "$dir/kit/git-push-guard.sh" "$RUNNER_TEMP/git-probe" && chmod +x "$RUNNER_TEMP/git-probe"
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/git-probe" version >/dev/null 2>&1 \
            || { echo "::error::kit git-push-guard.sh does not execute (probe failed) at $ref"; exit 1; }

      - name: "Fetch factory-setup (dmtools-agents releases — no tree checkout)"
        # Owner mandate 2026-10-03: the factory NEVER clones the
        # dmtools-agents tree. The workflow glue the run needs —
        # setup/ toolbelt (install.sh, cache.sh, review-verdict.sh,
        # fa-session.sh, ...), scripts/git-push-guard.sh fallback and the
        # four legacy leg configs — ships as the factory-setup-*.zip
        # release asset (built by ci/release_packs.mjs, rides every
        # agents-rel-* tag).
        # Compat: a pre-mounted factory-agents/ tree still WINS over the
        # zip — hosts that intentionally mount the tree (dmtools-agents'
        # own factory-probe, forks pinning local trees) keep their copies.
        # FACTORY_ROOT carries the winner for every later step.
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          PACK_TAG: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY }}
          # awf#25: AGENTS_VERSION is the documented pin knob (same
          # semantics as factory-sm.yml) — when pinned to a concrete
          # agents-rel-* tag it takes PRECEDENCE over the registry
          # variable for the setup pack AND the runtime pack registry.
          AGENTS_KNOB: ${{ vars.AGENTS_VERSION || 'latest' }}
        # Body: scripts/fetch-factory-setup.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/fetch-factory-setup.sh"

      - name: "Resolve parent config (pack launch.json wins, tree fallback)"
        # Wave 2 (owner 2026-10-01): teammate packs are self-sufficient —
        # the unpacked pack's launch.json IS the launch contract and WINS
        # over the legacy tree copy. Pack cache root (dmtools
        # AgentPackResolver): ~/.dmtools/packs/<agent>-<version>/ —
        # populated by `dmtools run` resolving a <agent>@latest parent, so
        # it is visible here on persistent-HOME/self-hosted runners and to
        # every step AFTER the agent run; fresh hosted runners fall back to
        # the legacy tree config until the run unpacks the pack. Neither
        # source present ⇒ loud fail (old pin without tree configs and
        # without a Wave-2 pack). fa-session.sh/run-agent.sh derive the
        # agent identity from the pack DIR, so naming stays stable either
        # way. Plain bash: GitLab-portable.
        env:
          LEGACY_CONFIG: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.config }}
        # Body: scripts/resolve-parent-config.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/resolve-parent-config.sh"

      - name: Export fa session identity + cache keys
        # AI_TEAMMATE_CONFIG_FILE comes from the resolve step above
        # (pack launch.json wins) via GITHUB_ENV.
        env:
          AI_TEAMMATE_DISPLAY_KEY: GH-${{ needs.guard.outputs.anchor }}
          AI_TEAMMATE_CONCURRENCY_KEY: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.anchor }}
        run: bash "${FACTORY_ROOT}/setup/cache.sh" keys fa-session

      - name: Restore fa session (resume the ticket conversation)
        # actions/cache saves are denied on issues-event runs (job token is
        # cache-read-only there), so the session tree rides a dedicated git
        # branch per issue; the per-issue concurrency group serializes writers.
        env:
          FA_SESS_BRANCH: fa-sess/${{ needs.guard.outputs.anchor }}
        # Body: scripts/restore-fa-session.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/restore-fa-session.sh"

      - name: Cache fa CLI (by version)
        if: env.FA_VERSION != 'latest'
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.local/bin/fa
            ~/lib
          key: fa-${{ env.FA_VERSION }}-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}

      - name: Resolve dmtools CLI version (latest -> current tag)
        # 'latest' (or empty) resolves to the current release tag so the
        # version-locked install.sh URL keeps working; owner mandate
        # 2026-10-01: machine legs always track the latest CLI/agents.
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        # Body: scripts/resolve-dmtools-version.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/resolve-dmtools-version.sh"

      - name: Cache dmtools CLI (by version)
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: ~/.dmtools/bin
          key: dmtools-${{ env.DMTOOLS_VERSION }}-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}

      - name: "Install prerequisites (fa; no-op on cache hit)"
        # Authenticated gh api download first — anonymous release-asset
        # downloads hit GitHub edge caches that served stale 404s for hours
        # after a re-cut release (observed 2026-09-12).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        # Body: scripts/install-fa-cli.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/install-fa-cli.sh"

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (pinned release bundle)
        # The installer ships as a release asset, version-locked to the
        # bundle it installs — no copy of install.sh in the target repo.
        # Body: scripts/install-dmtools-cli.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/install-dmtools-cli.sh"

      # flutter-action treats a literal version string strictly — the words
      # stable/beta/main/master are CHANNELS and crash the action ("Unable
      # to determine Flutter version for channel: stable", live: gh-623 run
      # 35370007049). Two steps with plain if-comparisons — the GH parser
      # rejects map-indexing expressions inside with:.
      - name: Set up Flutter for agent work (channel)
        if: inputs.flutter-version == 'stable' || inputs.flutter-version == 'beta' || inputs.flutter-version == 'main' || inputs.flutter-version == 'master'
        uses: subosito/flutter-action@v2
        with:
          channel: ${{ inputs.flutter-version }}
          cache: true

      - name: Set up Flutter for agent work (pinned version)
        if: inputs.flutter-version != '' && !(inputs.flutter-version == 'stable' || inputs.flutter-version == 'beta' || inputs.flutter-version == 'main' || inputs.flutter-version == 'master')
        uses: subosito/flutter-action@v2
        with:
          flutter-version: ${{ inputs.flutter-version }}
          cache: true

      - name: Verify prerequisites
        env:
          FLUTTER_VERSION: ${{ inputs.flutter-version }}
        # Body: scripts/verify-prerequisites.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/verify-prerequisites.sh"

      - name: Configure Git Author + push credentials
        # Purge the checkout's App token and make SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN the
        # credential that wins for github.com pushes (all logic in the
        # shared installer — one copy serves every push path in the job).
        env:
          SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: bash "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/kit/install-source-git-credentials.sh" 2>/dev/null \
            || bash "${FACTORY_ROOT}/setup/install-source-git-credentials.sh"

      - name: Trace git credential stack (push-time evidence)
        # gh-63 Task 1 — same run that pushes, right before the agent.
        # What each section proves:
        #   --show-origin        WHERE each credential source lives; the
        #                        extraheader section must come back empty —
        #                        asserted below, so any resurrection of the
        #                        App-token header (checkout layout change,
        #                        mid-run config write) fails the run here
        #                        instead of silently re-arming bot pushes
        #   submodule foreach    same proof for each submodule local config
        #                        (checkout arms those with submodules: true)
        #   git credential fill  dry-runs the exact push-path resolution and
        #                        shows the winning username; the password is
        #                        masked, and the helper's stderr line confirms
        #                        SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN served the credential
        env:
          SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        # Body: scripts/trace-git-credentials.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/trace-git-credentials.sh"

      - name: Seed local git excludes (factory workspace artifacts)
        # Everything the factory/agent scribbles into the workspace that must
        # NEVER reach a commit (agents run `git add -A`). .git/info/exclude is
        # local-only by construction — no .gitignore pollution in agent PRs.
        # Body: scripts/seed-git-excludes.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/seed-git-excludes.sh"

      - name: Write the issue into the agent input folder
        if: inputs.pr == ''
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          NUMBER: ${{ inputs.issue }}
        # Body: scripts/write-input-issue.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/write-input-issue.sh"

      - name: Write the PR into the agent input folder (PR-anchored runs)
        # #687: the PR is the anchor — the pr-N contextId is what the agent
        # scripts key on; ticket.json carries the same tracker-contract
        # shape so hydration paths stay uniform.
        if: inputs.pr != ''
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ inputs.pr }}
        # Body: scripts/write-input-pr.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/write-input-pr.sh"

      - name: Mark machine job started (issue task list)
        # Deterministic start marker in the issue body — survives agent
        # crashes/timeouts because the DONE twin below runs on always().
        # Contract: a "## Machine jobs" section with one task-list line per
        # factory run; the line's run URL is the unique id used to flip it.
        # PR-anchored runs skip it: no issue body to carry the task list.
        if: inputs.pr == ''
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || github.token }}
          NUMBER: ${{ inputs.issue }}
          JOB_LEG: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.kind }}
          RUNNER: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.runner }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        # Body: scripts/mark-job-started.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/mark-job-started.sh"

      - name: Export custom provider key slots (1-3) → job env
        # Generic numbered slots (owner decision 2026-10-13): the factory
        # never hardcodes provider key names — the caller stub maps each
        # slot from a plain repo secret and names the env var it lands as
        # (the stub comment documents the slot→key mapping). Values ride
        # the secrets context → runner-masked natively in every log; empty
        # slots are skipped, half-configured slots warn.
        env:
          CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY1: ${{ secrets.CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY1 }}
          CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY1_NAME: ${{ inputs.CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY1_NAME }}
          CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY2: ${{ secrets.CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY2 }}
          CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY2_NAME: ${{ inputs.CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY2_NAME }}
          CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY3: ${{ secrets.CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY3 }}
          CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY3_NAME: ${{ inputs.CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEY3_NAME }}
        # Body: scripts/export-provider-key-slots.sh (stage-1 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/export-provider-key-slots.sh"

      - name: Run agent (fa provider via runner env overrides)
        id: run_agent
        # Hard cap under the job's 260 min: a hung agent session must FAIL
        # the leg (the always() post-actions then run inside the remaining
        # budget and the red path re-queues) instead of the job-level
        # timeout killing everything mid-post-action. NOT 45: a real fix is
        # a 40-80 minute session (gh-623 was killed mid-work at exactly 61).
        # NOT 110: dev legs over Flutter sources run the analyzer + the
        # full flutter test suite — fa gh-1077 was killed mid-work at
        # exactly 110 (live flutter_tester orphans at teardown, PR step
        # never reached) — 2026-09-30.
        timeout-minutes: 240
        env:
          CI_RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          RUNNER: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.runner }}
          AI_AGENT_PROVIDER: fa
          # AI_TEAMMATE_CONFIG_FILE rides GITHUB_ENV from the resolve step
          # (pack launch.json wins, legacy tree fallback).
          AI_TEAMMATE_DISPLAY_KEY: GH-${{ needs.guard.outputs.anchor }}
          AI_TEAMMATE_CONCURRENCY_KEY: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.anchor }}
          ZAI_CODE_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZAI_CODE_KEY }}
          KIMI_REVIEW_KEY: ${{ secrets.KIMI_REVIEW_KEY }}
          SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # Agent-pack registry base (dm.ai #579): runners may parent packs
          # by REGISTRY ref (`pr_review@latest`) — the resolver reads the
          # releases base (incl. catalog.json) from this env. Callers set
          # the repo VARIABLE to their pinned dmtools-agents release tag;
          # unset (or empty) keeps the previous file-only behavior and the
          # resolver fails with an explicit "no pack registry" error.
          DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY }}
          # gh operations inside the session must act AS the SOURCE account:
          # events created with GITHUB_TOKEN do not trigger workflows.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || github.token }}
        run: |
          # awf#25 pin parity: when the setup resolved a concrete
          # agents-rel-* tag, the runtime registry base must point at
          # THAT release (catalog + zips + .sha256 sidecars), not the
          # floating repo variable — otherwise `<agent>@latest` refs
          # bypass the pin and a broken newest release takes down pinned
          # fleets (live: fa pr-1350 review leg 2026-10-06). Mirrors
          # factory-sm.yml's tick export and merge-trigger's derive.
          if [ -n "${RESOLVED_AGENTS_TAG:-}" ]; then
            export DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY="https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/releases/download/${RESOLVED_AGENTS_TAG}"
            echo "→ pack registry pinned to ${RESOLVED_AGENTS_TAG} (AGENTS_VERSION parity, awf#25)"
          fi
          # #542 mechanical guard: interpose the git push/commit guard shim at
          # the FRONT of PATH before `dmtools run` so EVERY push path in the
          # session is covered — both the fa agent's own shell tool (inherits
          # the dmtools process env) and the JS pre/post-actions'
          # cli_execute_command (PATH-resolved `git`). Refuses pushes to
          # main/master/default branch and closing keywords in commit
          # messages. Deliberately NOT written to $GITHUB_PATH: later workflow
          # steps (session-branch persistence) push legitimately.
          GIT_GUARD_BIN="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/git-push-guard-bin"
          mkdir -p "${GIT_GUARD_BIN}"
          GUARD="${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/kit/git-push-guard.sh"
          [ -f "$GUARD" ] || GUARD="${FACTORY_ROOT}/scripts/git-push-guard.sh"
          ln -sf "$GUARD" "${GIT_GUARD_BIN}/git"
          export PATH="${GIT_GUARD_BIN}:${PATH}"
          git --version  # resolves through the shim — proves the wiring
          # FULL session trace: FA_LOG_FILE tees every line fa prints to the
          # file, uploaded as an artifact below; dmtools mirrors child output
          # live to its own stderr, so the agent's work streams into the log.
          FA_LOG_FILE="${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/.dmtools/fa-trace.log"
          export FA_LOG_FILE
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "${FA_LOG_FILE}")"
          touch "${FA_LOG_FILE}"
          echo "fa full trace: ${FA_LOG_FILE}"
          # Body: scripts/dmtools-selfheal.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
          # SOURCED so the healed PATH propagates to the rest of the step).
          . "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/dmtools-selfheal.sh"
          RUN_OUTPUT="${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/.dmtools/run-output.txt"
          # #687: machine login rides jobParams so PR-anchored verdicts arm
          # the merge pipeline regardless of what the checked-out branch's
          # .dmtools/config.js carries (postPRReviewComments reads
          # jobParams.machineAuthor first).
          DMTOOLS_ARGS=()
          MA='${{ inputs.machine-author }}'
          if [ -n "$MA" ]; then
            DMTOOLS_ARGS+=('{"params":{"jobParams":{"machineAuthor":"'"$MA"'"}}}')
          fi
          # Body: scripts/fa-trace-watchdog.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
          # backgrounded like the inline `( ... ) &` subshell it replaces).
          RUN_OUTPUT="${RUN_OUTPUT}" bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/fa-trace-watchdog.sh" &
          WATCHDOG_PID=$!
          # Body: scripts/stall-capture.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
          # backgrounded like the inline `( ... ) &` subshell it replaces).
          bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/stall-capture.sh" &
          STALL_MON_PID=$!
          trap 'kill "${WATCHDOG_PID}" "${STALL_MON_PID}" 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
          dmtools run "${RUNNER}" ${DMTOOLS_ARGS[@]+"${DMTOOLS_ARGS[@]}"} \
            --metadata '{"contextId":"${{ needs.guard.outputs.anchor }}"}' \
            --ciRunUrl "${CI_RUN_URL}" --debug 2>&1 | tee "${RUN_OUTPUT}"
          RC=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
          exit "${RC}"

      - name: Publish leg token usage (fa-tokens ledger -> factory-data)
        # Factory-board token spend (dmtools-agents#781 producer side): the
        # fa CLI prints a `fa-tokens:` ledger line per session segment into
        # the run output; sum them and append one row per leg under
        # data/fa-tokens.json on the factory-data branch — the shape the SM
        # tick's fetchTokensFromBranch consumes (card.tokens rows
        # {leg, at, prompt, completion, total}, key 'pr-N'/'issue-N').
        # Tokens are decorative: ANY miss (no ledger line, 404 first
        # publish, conflict after retries) warns and moves on — this step
        # must never redden a green leg nor gate a failed one. always():
        # the cost happened even when the agent run above failed/timed out.
        if: always()
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          ANCHOR: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.anchor }}
          KIND: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.kind }}
          CONFIG: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.config }}
          RUN_OUTPUT: ${{ github.workspace }}/.dmtools/run-output.txt
          DATA_BRANCH: factory-data
          DATA_PATH: data/fa-tokens.json
        # Body: scripts/publish-token-usage.sh (stage-1 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/publish-token-usage.sh"

      - name: Mark machine job done (issue task list)
        # always(): the checkbox flips even when the agent run above timed
        # out, was cancelled, or failed — the marker can never dangle.
        # PR-anchored runs skip it (no issue task list).
        if: always() && inputs.pr == ''
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || github.token }}
          NUMBER: ${{ inputs.issue }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          JOB_RESULT: ${{ job.status }}
        # Body: scripts/mark-job-done.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/mark-job-done.sh"

      - name: Apply the review verdict (review runs only)
        # Zero-maintainer keystone: convert the review agent's verdict into
        # the label that drives the next machine step.
        #   APPROVE (+ green CI on the PR head) → pr_approved → merge
        #   CHANGES_REQUESTED / BLOCK           → agent:rework (bounded)
        # Verdict extraction walks a fallback chain (gh-305: the old silent
        # skip stranded the cycle post-review — no REQUEST_CHANGES → rework,
        # no approval → merge):
        #   pr_review.json → run output → machine-written PR comments →
        #   machine-written issue comments → LOUD failure
        # No verdict anywhere ⇒ ::error:: + needs-human + per-source
        # diagnosis comment + exit 1 (the cycle is stranded; a human must
        # label it). gh calls stay in this step; the parser stays pure —
        # pack loop/verdict.sh first (Wave 2), legacy tree
        # factory-agents/setup/review-verdict.sh fallback.
        # The CI-green gate applies to the APPROVE path only: gating rework
        # on green CI would deadlock exactly when CI is red because the code
        # needs rework. A PAT is REQUIRED for labeling (mute GITHUB_TOKEN).
        if: needs.guard.outputs.kind == 'review' && inputs.pr == ''
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          NUMBER: ${{ inputs.issue }}
          RUN_OUTPUT: .dmtools/run-output.txt
          MACHINE_AUTHOR: ${{ inputs.machine-author }}
          MAX_ROUNDS: ${{ env.MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS }}
        # Engine-side since dmtools-agents#935: the verdict application is SM
        # cycle logic and ships in the factory-setup zip (pack
        # agents-rel-20261016-185247+). The awf copy is gone — this is the
        # only source now (ordered flip: pack landed first).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-setup/scripts/apply-review-verdict.sh"

      - name: Close the review cycle (review runs only)
        # A review run must never re-queue itself: strip the queue label at
        # completion (removing a label fires no `labeled` event).
        if: always() && needs.guard.outputs.kind == 'review' && inputs.pr == ''
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          NUMBER: ${{ inputs.issue }}
        # Body: scripts/close-review-cycle.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/close-review-cycle.sh"

      - name: Close the rework cycle (rework runs only)
        # Symmetric strip: a stale agent:rework would silently swallow every
        # later CI-failure re-arm (and any human re-label). #544: on
        # PR-anchored rework the label lives on the PR, not on an issue.
        if: always() && contains(needs.guard.outputs.runner, 'rework')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          NUMBER: ${{ inputs.issue }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ inputs.pr }}
        # Body: scripts/close-rework-cycle.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/close-rework-cycle.sh"

      - name: Persist fa project memory into the repository
        # fa project memory (.fah/memory) committed back = agent knowledge
        # accumulates in the repository. Best-effort on protected branches.
        if: always()
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        # Body: scripts/persist-fa-memory.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/persist-fa-memory.sh"

      - name: Quarantine poisoned fa session
        # Owner RCA (dmd PR-266, 2026-09-27): the session store's dark side.
        # A leg whose fa session hangs mid-run gets cancelled; the persist
        # step below (always()) then SAVES the frozen session, and the
        # restore step at the top of the NEXT leg re-loads it — three
        # consecutive zombie legs resumed the same poisoned state (fa
        # trace silent from the first minute of each) until the
        # fa-sess/<anchor> branch was deleted by hand. The persist step is
        # right that a failed run's session is valuable context — unless
        # the session itself is the suspect. Fa streams every turn into
        # FA_LOG_FILE, so a trace silent for the last N minutes of a
        # failed/cancelled leg means the session stopped making progress;
        # then: move the store aside (the persist step finds nothing and
        # early-exits) AND delete fa-sess/<anchor> — otherwise the next
        # leg restores the poison anyway. A leg that failed with an ACTIVE
        # trace (a real error mid-work) keeps its session for the retry.
        # Runs before the trace-artifact upload so the quarantined store
        # ships with the diagnostics.
        if: always() && (steps.run_agent.outcome == 'failure' || steps.run_agent.outcome == 'cancelled')
        env:
          FA_SESS_BRANCH: fa-sess/${{ needs.guard.outputs.anchor }}
          SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          AGENT_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.run_agent.outcome }}
        # Body: scripts/quarantine-fa-session.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/quarantine-fa-session.sh"

      - name: Collect fa crash log (uncaught errors live outside the workspace)
        # fa's last-resort handler appends uncaught errors (e.g. the
        # "StreamSink is bound to a stream" abort-path crash on the hung
        # dmd PR-266 legs) to $HOME/.fah/crash.log — outside the workspace,
        # invisible to the artifact below. Copy it in, best-effort.
        if: always()
        # Body: scripts/collect-fa-crash-log.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/collect-fa-crash-log.sh"

      - name: Upload the full fa session trace
        # AFTER the memory-persist push: the artifact must include the final
        # helper invocation of the run.
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: fa-trace-${{ needs.guard.outputs.anchor }}-${{ github.run_id }}
          path: |
            .dmtools/fa-trace.log
            .dmtools/run-output.txt
            .dmtools/credential-helper.log
            .dmtools/stall-capture.log
            .dmtools/fa-crash.log
            .dmtools/fa-sessions-quarantine/**
          if-no-files-found: ignore

      - name: Persist fa session to its git branch
        # The save side of the git-based session store; runs even on failure
        # (a failed run's session is exactly the context the next rework
        # round needs). Best-effort.
        if: always()
        env:
          FA_SESS_BRANCH: fa-sess/${{ needs.guard.outputs.anchor }}
          SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          ANCHOR: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.anchor }}
          CONFIG: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.config }}
        # Body: scripts/persist-fa-session.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/persist-fa-session.sh"

      - name: Hand the issue to the reviewer (dev runs only)
        # Remove-then-add agent:review so the `labeled` event always fires
        # (re-adding an existing label is event-wise a no-op); agent:rework
        # goes too — the guard routes on it with priority over review.
        if: needs.guard.outputs.kind == 'dev' && inputs.pr == ''
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          NUMBER: ${{ inputs.issue }}
        # Body: scripts/hand-issue-to-reviewer.sh (stage-2 de-bloat — byte-extracted, behavior-identical;
        # delivered via the factory-kit fetch at the invocation ref).
        run: bash -e "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/scripts/hand-issue-to-reviewer.sh"

      - name: Link the run back to the issue
        if: always() && inputs.pr == ''
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          NUMBER: ${{ inputs.issue }}
          OUTCOME: ${{ job.status }}
          CI_RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          gh issue comment "$NUMBER" --body \
            "🤖 AI Teammate run ${OUTCOME}: ${CI_RUN_URL:-$GITHUB_SERVER_URL/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs/$GITHUB_RUN_ID}"

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# ROLLOUT SCOPE (this phase): the loop reacts ONLY to artifacts authored
# by the machine itself — issues opened by `ai-teammate` and PRs opened
# by `ai-teammate`. Human-created issues (even labeled/assigned to the

#   issue labeled while assigned     → factory, leg derived by the guard
#   PR opened by ai-teammate         → factory, leg=review on the linked
#                                      issue (parsed from the PR body)
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual)  → leg pinned by input
#
# ALL loop logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
# event triggers, the author filter, the PR→issue resolution, the
# per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.

# Secrets (explicit mapping): SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required by the factory),

name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      ((github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' &&

      format('{0} · gh-{1}: {2}',
        github.event.action == 'assigned' && '⚒️ dev (assigned handoff)' || 'machine loop',
        github.event.issue.number, github.event.issue.title) }}

on:

    # assigned only — labeled REMOVED (2026-10-01): every label echo (the dev
    # leg's own status:In Development, SM backfills) spawned a queued twin run
    # behind the per-issue concurrency group (live dmd gh-317/gh-318); the
    # in-run dedupe cannot act — workflow-level concurrency holds the whole
    # run pending before any job starts. Leg dispatching is dispatch-only
    # (SM workflow_dispatch; manual rework override #544 = dispatch leg=rework).

    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored review runs (#687) — the SM dispatches review with pr instead of issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

# the real rights (SEC-08 review #849, thread -1oD — a top-level write block
# becomes the default for every future job in this workflow). The factory
# job's own permissions block mirrors the pinned callee's declared scopes
# (factory-teammate.yml declares contents/issues/pull-requests/actions
# write): a reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above the CALLING JOB's
# effective grant, so an explicit read-only block ON THE CALLING JOB made
# every call fail validation with startup_failure (live bisect,
# 2026-09-18) — the job-scoped mirror is the minimal consistent set (SEC-08,
# #796).
permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-266');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
